question: Where does PL/M-80 V4.0 place and how does it address one local BYTE in a parameterless procedure?

toolchain.simulator: z80pack Intel Intellec MDS-800 Simulator Release 1.39
toolchain.overlay_provenance_note: The local recipe labels PLM80 and OV0-OV4 V4.0 and OV5-OV6 V3.1. Individual overlay opens were not traced; actual per-run overlay use remains unresolved.

commands: COPY each LOCVAR artifact TO :HP: and capture from /tmp/.z80pack/intelmdssim.pt

paper_tape_capture.observed_framing_per_file: 120 zero leader bytes + file payload + 120 zero trailer bytes
paper_tape_capture.normalization: strip the zero leader and truncate to the exact payload byte count reported by ISIS-II DIR; all removed trailer bytes were zero

direct_observations: Listing cross-reference gives LOCAL offset 0000H and size 1; compiler reports VARIABLE area size 0001H.
Locator assigns the one-byte DATA area to 369CH. P executes LXI H,369CH; MVI M,2AH, so this sample stores the assigned byte at that absolute address, not on the procedure stack.
MAIN initializes SP to 369CH, calls P at 3688H, then executes EI and HLT. The CALL return address is 3686H; P ends in RET.
Maximum STACK is 2 bytes; listing attributes 2 to MAIN and 0 to P.
LINK map includes LOCVAR.OBJ(MAIN) alone; PLM80.LIB was not needed for this program.
interpretation_limit: These are observations about one procedure with one BYTE local assigned a constant. They do not establish local allocation behavior for recursion, reentrancy, arrays, other storage classes, or other compiler versions.
unresolved_questions: The local mixed-overlay recipe's individual PLM80 overlay provenance and whether OV5/OV6 were opened remain unverified.
This fixture does not establish allocation behavior for recursive/reentrant procedures or other local-variable forms.
